item.title: DMI/MEMS Seminar Presented by Prof Bharat Jalan — Wed Nov 18, 12:00 PM — Fitzpatrick Center Schiciano Auditorium Side A
item.description:
Abstract: Progress in condensed-matter physics ultimately depends on materials reality. Many long-standing questions arise not from a lack of theoretical ideas, but from the challenge of controlling defects, disorder, stoichiometry, and strain in real materials. In this talk, I will discuss altermagnetism in RuO2 - a rutile 4d transition-metal oxide - from the perspective of materials synthesis.
Using chemistry-guided, atomically controlled epitaxial growth, we systematically tune strain and materials quality in RuO2 thin films, including films approaching the unit-cell limit while retaining metallicity. This materials control enables us to distinguish intrinsic electronic and magnetic behavior from effects arising from defects, relaxation, and structural inhomogeneity. In this course, you have the opportunity to delve into how each one of us experience the physical, emotional and behavioral signs and symptoms of burnout in our lifetimes. item.description:
AGS invites you to a discussion of foreign policy and the future of the Republican Party after the 2026 Midterm Elections with CBS News national security analyst and host of the School of War podcast Aaron MacLean.
Aaron MacLean is one of the nation's leading experts in national security and foreign policy. He currently hosts the School of War podcast, contributes as a national security analyst on CBS News, and serves as dean of Hertog Security Studies. After serving as a Marine for seven years, Mr. MacLean was the senior foreign policy advisor for Senator Tome Cotton (R-AR) and a Senior Fellow at the Hudson Institute. Mr. MacLean earned a B.A. in philosophy and the history of mathematics from St. John's College, Annapolis, and an M.Phil. (Dist.) in medieval Arabic from the University of Oxford. In 2013 he received the Apgar Award for Excellence in Teaching while serving on the faculty of the United States Naval Academy.

item.title: Immediate and Longer-run Impacts of Universal Health Insurance: Evidence on Child Height in Mexico — Thu Nov 19, 12:00 PM — SSRI-Gross Hall 270
item.description: Abstract: Universal public health insurance programs are being implemented across the globe, putting enormous pressure on public finances, even as their impacts on population health and economic growth are not well-established. We exploit the roll-out of Seguro Popular, which provided public health insurance to about half of Mexico's population, in combination with the biology of human linear growth, to identify the causal impact of universal health insurance on child height, an indicator of longer-run nutritional status correlated with adult health, human capital, and productivity. Using longitudinal, population-representative data from the Mexican Family Life Survey, we establish that, overall, Seguro Popular had, at best, a modest impact on child height when first introduced. However, program effects increase over time and are large and significantly positive several years after the program has been established. item.title: British India and British North America in the Age of Revolutions: Parallel and Connected Histories — Thu Nov 19, 1:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
The history of the rise of British India and the fall of British America after the Seven Years War (1756-63) used, until recently, to be considered parallel but separate histories, driven by essentially different regional dynamics and studied by different tribes of historians. This talk explores the rise of global approaches to the connected history of British imperialism in Asia and the Atlantic World, and asks what new directions connected, trans-regional histories of this period might take in the future.
Robert Travers is Professor of History and Director of the South Asia Program at Cornell. He is the author of two books about colonial state formation in eastern India in the late eighteenth century, Ideology and Empire in Eighteenth Century India: The British in Bengal (Cambridge, 2007), and Empires of Complaints. item.description: Bioactive by Design: Engineering Biomaterials for Tissue Regeneration Advances in biomaterial design and its impact on biological function has shown promise in the field of regenerative medicine. This presentation will describe biomaterial properties and designs that impart cues to stem cells and other cell types to affect their behavior and tissue formation in vitro and in vivo. item.title: Scratching the Witch via Adaptation Dramaturgy: Jen Silverman's "Witch" — Thu Nov 19, 3:00 PM — None
item.description: What itches do we scratch by putting witch hunts onstage? In this talk, Jane Barnette considers the palimpsestuous pleasures made possible by Jen Silverman's 21st-century "riff" on The Witch of Edmondton, a five-act tragicomedy from 1621 that itself was based on "a known true story." Written by William Rowley, Thomas Dekker, and John Ford (among other poets) and performed by a company of at least twelve actors playing approximately thirty roles, the Jacobian tale adapted popular ballads and pamphlets from that same year, offering salacious gossip about a local woman, Elizabeth Sawyer, who was executed upon confessing to witchcraft. Silverman's play is like a stovetop reduction--by slowly simmering the sprawling 17th-century play, the playwright thickens the sauce, intensifying its flavor and revealing the story's essence for present-day audiences. item.description:

item.title: Joint Invasive Removal with Wake Audubon (Fuquay-Varina) — Wed Nov 18, 9:00 AM
item.description:
NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter is partners with Wake Audubon’s ongoing project to conserve and support the natural heritage of a unique nature park in Fuquay-Varina, the Carroll Howard Johnson Environmental Education Park. The NC Natural Heritage Progam lists portions of this site as 7 out of 10 for natural diversity, which is exceptional for a suburban/urban location. Our first and second effort this year was incredibly effective and we look forward to the third one being the same. Our teams cut or pull the invasives and haul them out by the parking lot. Fuquay Varina Public Works loads all this into large trailers and hauls it away as they are filled. Last time, we filled two trailers, and there is plenty more to go! We suggest that folks wear long sleeved shirts and pants and bring gloves and water. Tools are provided, but feel free to bring any favorite personal tools as well. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.description: 5 Points Gallery, an artist-owned contemporary art gallery in downtown Durham, is pleased to announce an exhibition of paintings by Featured Artist King Nobuyoshi Godwin, whose vibrant, imaginative work reflects his experience of autism and synesthesia. Bringing together expressive animals, vivid colors, and numbers that convey emotion, Godwin creates playful worlds filled with unexpected connections. In a painting inspired by the African shoebill, King transforms the imposing bird into a potential friend, welcoming it into his colorful world of unlikely companions. item.title: The Imprint of Faith: Exhibition Opening at Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar — Fri Nov 20, 6:00 PM — Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar
item.description:
Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar is proud to present The Imprint of Faith: What Has Been Given, What Has Been Taken. Faith. Religion. Worship. Spirituality. Each has left an imprint on many of our lives, often by shaping our communities, our cultures, and even our mental health. For some, faith has given hope, peace, belonging, and resilience. For others, it has been twisted with trauma, shame, exclusion, or loss. Sometimes, it is both. As artists, we have the opportunity to explore and share these experiences through a multitude of mediums and ideas. Through art, we can examine the ways faith and spirituality have influenced our identities, relationships, and understanding of the world. During this holiday season, we aim to support thoughtful conversation through art. What has faith, religion or spirituality given you? What has it taken away? How has it changed the way you see yourself and the world around you?
Source: Downtown Durham Inc
